name: Pay approved supplier bills on or before their due date, once
outcome: Each approved supplier bill has left the business's account on or before its due date, to the bank details the supplier actually gave, in the right currency, exactly once, recorded against the bill it settles.
description: Accounts payable as an execution job: scheduling and releasing payment for bills somebody has already approved. It is not fin.match-invoices-to-orders, which decides whether a bill should be paid at all by matching it to the order and the receipt; that decision is upstream and has its own id. It is not fin.send-payouts, which pays earnings, balances and entitlements to many recipients who are not suppliers sending bills. It is not fin.forecast-cash, which says whether the money will be there. Paying once, to details that were not changed by someone impersonating the supplier, is part of the outcome and not a detail: duplicate and misdirected payments are this job's characteristic failures, and a solution that cannot show it prevents them has not done it.
measures: share of bills paid on or before the due date
duplicate or misdirected payments per thousand sent
early payment discounts captured against those offered
days from approval to money leaving the account
payment runs released without a person re-keying an amount
